items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 22 at 4:30AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
items.description:
Areas of fog will continue across parts of southeast Georgia and
northeast Florida through the early morning hours. Patchy dense
fog is expected which will reduce visibilities to less than 1/2
mile on roadways at times. Fog should then dissipate by mid
morning, by 10 AM. It is possible fog could become dense over
more locations which would require a dense fog advisory.

The nature of the fog is such that visibilities will vary greatly
over short distances. If driving this morning, slow down, use
low-beam headlights and leave extra distance between you and the
vehicle in front of you.

items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 22 at 1:20AM EST until November 23 at 5:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
items.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Coastal Duval County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through this evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 5 AM EST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

items.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 22 at 3:26AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
items.description:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Coastal waters from Altamaha Sound to Fernandina Beach FL out 20
NM...
Coastal waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL out 20 NM...

Patchy to areas of fog are expected along the coastal areas of
southeast Georgia and pars of northeast Florida and may extend out to
10 or 15 NM from shore. Localized dense fog with visibility at or
below 1 NM is possible.
items.instruction:
Dense fog may reducing visibilities to below 1 NM. Reduce your speed
and keep a lookout for other vessels, buoys, and breakwaters. Keep
your navigation lights on. If not equipped with radar, you should
consider seeking safe harbor.
